Incorporating the Beige Book for the May 2018 FOMC cycle strengthens the cautiously positive read. District reports characterized growth as modest to moderate, with tight labor markets and increasing reports of worker shortages, modest-to-moderate wage gains, and slightly firmer price pressures. Business activity and manufacturing were broadly solid, while consumer spending was mixed (notably softer autos) and housing faced inventory and cost constraints. Credit conditions were generally steady, with healthy business loan demand but some tighter standards in consumer categories and mixed CRE trends.

This aligns closely with the FOMC’s “moderate” expansion, strong labor market, and near-2% inflation narrative, and it echoes the SLOOS signal of easier C&I but tighter consumer credit. The Beige Book thus modestly reinforces the growth outlook via business activity and hiring, while still flagging sectoral frictions (autos, housing, CRE pockets) and rising input costs that argue for gradualism and balanced risks.

Net: a slightly firmer positive tilt than the SLOOS/FSR-only read, but still tempered by consumer/CRE caution and cost pressures.
